To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) conformity with the norms is associated with greater identification with a self-defining group, and (b) greater identification with a relevant group is associated with more positive emotional responses to conformity than violation of norms.

(a) greater identification with the group is associated with more positive emotion for members who conform with versus violate the group’s injunctive norms and (b) greater identification is associated with more positivity for members who conform versus violate the group's identity-relevant descriptive norms.

(a) conformity to the norms of self-relevant groups elicits positive emotions, whereas violations of those norms lead to negative emotions, (b) these effects are found for both injunctive and descriptive norms, and (c) these effects are stronger for injunctive norms and for descriptive norms that are identity-relevant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the motivational processes that underlie normative behavior.
the role that social norms play in the formation and maintenance of social identity.
the motivational consequences of normative behavior and the processes by which norms acquire identity-relevance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the greater the identification, the more positive the emotions and self-evaluation following conformity to the group’s normative behavior.
the greater the degree of identification that an individual has with a group, the more positive emotions they experience when they conform to group norms, but not when they violate group norms.
conformity to norms is a function of social identity, and that this is particularly the case when the norm is injunctive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
social norms are a powerful force in our lives and that they are especially influential when they are relevant to the self.
the more a norm matters to you, the better you feel when you do what it tells you to do.
the greater the degree to which people identify with a particular group, the more they are likely to feel good when they conform to the norms of the group.
The main takeaway from our work is that
social norms can have an impact on our emotions.
the effects of social norms on behavior depend on the relevance of norms to one’s identity.
people conform to group norms because doing so is emotionally rewarding and self-enhancing.
